text.title: Remote 1:1 Async Fallback Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete `Async11Note` for a Warsaw PM and a Sydney IC in week 21, answered inside the window and acked the same day, with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad note showing what the validator prints and what the IC's manager sees beyond it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Olena (PM, Warsaw, UTC+2) and Taras (IC, Sydney, UTC+10) share no working hours. Their last synchronous call was in week 19, outside Olena's hours by rotation; weeks 20 and 21 are async. The pair's protocol was reviewed on 2026-04-07 with 11 of 12 cycles answered in the window. In week 21 Taras reports a stalled PR review and a pending token-TTL decision, and clarity down to 6 after the S14 scope changed twice.

example.title: olena.k--taras.v, cycle 2026-W21, answered and acked
example.note: `consecutive_async_cycles` is 2 with the last sync call in W19: this note is allowed, the W22 note would be the third and last before another call is booked (r-async-only-when-sync-infeasible).

The blockers prompt asks for a WBS id, the decisions prompt for an owner and a date, the morale prompt for the three pulse-survey axes on 1-10; Taras's answer "workload 7, autonomy 8, clarity 6" is comparable with the W17 answer (r-three-named-prompts-fixed).

Posted Monday 09:00 Sydney time, closing Wednesday 09:00 Sydney time: 48 business hours on the IC's clock, no weekend or holiday inside. The PM's Warsaw evening is irrelevant to the window (r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours).
All three fields are present, in the IC's words, with `authored_by: ic`; "none" in any field would also have counted as answered (r-empty-answer-ok-missing-field-is-unresponsive).

Received 16:30 Sydney, acked 18:00 Warsaw the same calendar day: 6 business hours, and one owned, sprint-dated action per reported item; nothing for the morale line, which is not a blocker (r-pm-ack-within-24h-with-owned-actions).
An in-window answer sets `unresponsive_count` to 0 regardless of history and `action: none` is the only valid value at 0 (r-escalation-ladder-reschedule-then-manager).
`channel.visible_to` is exactly the pair and the morale flag is false; the clarity-6 line lives only here (r-private-channel-morale-never-aggregated-by-name).

The April review rate is 11/12 = 0.9167, above 80%, so `structural_decision: none` is allowed; `last_reviewed` 2026-04-07 is 41 days before this posting, inside the 90-day window (r-quarterly-response-rate-review).

example.title: What the validator and the IC's manager reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.header.response_window_business_hours: 12 violates minimum=24`, `$.channel.morale_shared_outside_pair: must equal False, got True`, `$.sync_infeasibility.consecutive_async_cycles: 5 violates maximum=3`, `$.prompts.blockers: 'Anything to share this week?' does not match pattern '(?i)(wbs|ticket|id\b)'`, `$.prompts.blockers: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.prompts.decisions_needed: 'Any decisions pending?' does not match pattern '(?i)(whom|who|owner)'`, `$.prompts.morale: 'How is it going overall?' does not match pattern '(?i)workload'` (and the same for autonomy, clarity and 1-10), `$.escalation.manager_packet.includes_morale: must equal False, got True`, `$.escalation.action: must equal 'escalate_to_manager', got 'none'`.

Once those are fixed, the cross-field block reports: `posting.window_closes_at is 12h after posted_at; 48 business hours in the IC's timezone can never close sooner (r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours)`.

What the manager sees beyond the validator: a note posted at 17:00 Friday in Warsaw whose window closed at 13:00 Saturday in Sydney, three reminders over the IC's weekend, and a fifth consecutive async cycle. The "unresponsive" IC was never given a window they could meet, and the packet arriving on the manager's desk carries the IC's morale line, which is the moment every later morale answer on the team becomes a 7.
